reasons: Review independence and adequacy: the opus55-high verdict is short but grounded. Its test log shows the same binary hashes as the gate build (password_policy_964-293a71d62aa1e29a, auth_middleware-4572c4f192e795c4), each result line reads 0 failed, and minted-dbs.json lists qic_631_917_964_20261022_6 created 16:19:29Z inside the phase-2 window. I re-read the whole backend and frontend diff plus both untracked files myself and reached the same four findings with nothing added, which is what an independent second pass should look like.

Hard look at LOW-1 (change endpoint ordering): users.rs:1597 calls enforce before require_db (1598), find_by_id (1599) and verify_password (1605), so the behaviour is correct today. Every security-relevant invariant is pinned by a test I read: a refused change leaves the hash, both sessions and zero 'Password changed' notifications and the old password still logs in; wrong currentPassword with a compliant newPassword returns 401 with the hash unchanged; a weak but correct currentPassword is accepted for a compliant change, so the policy is provably not applied to currentPassword. If enforce were moved after verify_password the only observable change would be that wrong-current plus weak-new returns 401 instead of 400 with rule details: no credential exposure, no write, and that handler has no lockout or rate-limit path that the order could affect. Reset and sign-up ordering is already pinned by the state(None) tests, which would return a database error instead of 400 if the check moved. LOW is the right severity; not required before PUSH. A one-case test (wrong current plus 11-char new, expect 400 length and hash unchanged) is a cheap optional follow-up.

LOW-2: refused_signup_creates_no_user_and_compliant_signup_passes_the_policy asserts status != 400 but then asserts the user row exists and verify_password(COMPLIANT, stored hash) is true, so sign-up success is proven by database state even though the test SMTP-less environment returns 500 CONFIG_ERROR; LOW stands.

LOW-3: the change-password helper copy omits the symbol rule by the 917 design notes and PLAN-964 lines 134 and 153 explicitly accept this interim state (955 and 956 own the checklist). The server refuses with the symbol message and the page renders it (E-live-change-12-nosymbol.png, jest 'renders the server message'). The shared PasswordInput component still carries an 'At least 8 characters' checklist, but showStrength defaults to false and the reset page does not set it, so nothing on the reset page contradicts the new 12-character hint; E-live-reset-11.png shows the banner 'Password must be at least 12 characters' and the hint 'At least 12 characters'. 917 AC3 holds.

LOW-4: PasswordRule::id() and serde rename_all define the same five ids twice; rule_ids_serialize_as_camel_case_frontend_keys pins them equal. Correct DRY candidate, not a correctness or contract problem.

My own checks beyond the reviewer's: password_policy::enforce is called at exactly three sites (auth.rs:446 after SIGNUP_PER_IP, auth.rs:2808, users.rs:1597); the three validate(length) attributes are gone and no other server-side password length check remains; the other hash_password callers (admin create-user, test accounts, email OTP, backup codes) are out of scope by PLAN-964 line 134 and untouched; the only .expect() additions are inside auth.rs mod tests; no let _ =, .ok(), _ => or unwrap outside #[cfg(test)] in the diff and both gate suppression scans are empty; clippy finished; message strings and the error body are byte-identical to api-contract.md; PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH is consumed only by the reset page and ChangePasswordSection, so the login path and legacy sign-in are untouched (also pinned by legacy_passwords_below_the_policy_still_sign_in).

Acceptance rows: every locally provable 917 and 964 row maps to a test I read in tests/password_policy_964.rs, password_policy.rs unit tests or the two jest files; staging rows are left to QA with the throwaway-account rule stated in the acceptance map. The only row whose accepted-behaviour wording ('refused before current-password check') rests on source order rather than a test is 964-AC1c, which is LOW-1.

Receipt note, not blocking: the EXIT= lines in phase-2-review-opus.log are blank (exit code not captured), but each cargo and jest result line reads 0 failed and the binaries match the gate build.
